title: The World's Most Rewarding Wildlife Travel Experiences
paragraphs: For many travelers, seeing animals in the wild is the highlight of a trip. But which wildlife experiences are the most rewarding? A new ranking attempts to answer that question.

The ranking, called the Wildlife Experience Index 2026, was published by the travel company Bailey Robinson and reported in August 2026. It evaluated 30 wildlife experiences around the world based on six factors: how rare the animal is, how remote the location is, the importance of the species for conservation, how exclusive the experience is, how easy it is to reach and how likely visitors are to see the animal. Each factor was given a score out of 10, and these were combined into a total score out of 100.

At the top of the list, with a score of 90, was mountain gorilla trekking in Rwanda or Uganda. Access to the gorillas is strictly limited. In Rwanda, for example, only 96 permits are issued each day, while in Uganda's Bwindi National Park, only eight visitors per day are allowed to visit each family of gorillas. The experience received a perfect score for the chance of seeing the animals, as expert trackers help visitors find them.

In second place, with a score of 88.5, was an expedition to see emperor penguins in Antarctica, which received perfect scores for remoteness and exclusivity. Third was an expedition to see saiga antelopes in Kazakhstan, followed by tracking snow leopards in the Himalayas. The rest of the top 10 included tracking rhinos in Indonesia, Namibia or Kenya, seeing polar bears in Svalbard, meeting orangutans in Borneo and going on safari to see African wild dogs.
Notably, eight of the top 10 experiences involve threatened species, and most of the experiences on the list are in Asia and Africa.

Sarah Parker of Bailey Robinson said that what stood out was "the relationship between rarity and remoteness." She added that "The real luxury is the opportunity to experience something rare and meaningful, while travelling responsibly."
